configurePresets.name: conf-screentest-host-os-debug
configurePresets.description: The plain-Linux/Windows host build, and the ONLY configuration that registers this project's test suite. Distinct from conf-screentest-host-debug, which is a host build of the Pico SDK (pico_hostmode) and a different thing entirely. This tree was hand-configured for a long time and existed under no preset, so 'how do I run the tests' had no reproducible answer and CI had nothing to call. binaryDir matches the directory that already existed, so nobody's working tree is invalidated.

configurePresets.name: conf-screentest-waveshare-touch169-riscv-debug
configurePresets.description: Same board and same sources as conf-screentest-waveshare-touch169-debug, built for the RP2350's Hazard3 RISC-V cores instead of its Cortex-M33 pair. LIGHT_ARCH picks between the two archs the rp2350 chip entry registers, and light_resolve_pico_platform() turns that into PICO_PLATFORM=rp2350-riscv, from which pico-sdk selects its own RISC-V toolchain file. PICO_TOOLCHAIN_PATH is required rather than a convenience: the ARM trees find arm-none-eabi-gcc on PATH (PICO_TOOLCHAIN_PATH is empty in their caches) and there is only one PATH, so without it the SDK would search that same PATH for a riscv32-* compiler and find none. Setting it only here also keeps it out of the ARM trees. Compiler flags are left to pico-sdk's own probe, which selects the Zca/Zcb/Zcmp set -- see the vendor note.

cacheVariables._comment_PICO_TOOLCHAIN_PATH: read from the environment, never hardcoded -- light-env.ps1 sets it from the 'riscv-toolchain' entry in the gitignored user.config.ps1, or from <LIGHT_TOOLS_PATH>/riscv-toolchain*. The RISC-V toolchain is deliberately kept OFF PATH (it breaks the ARM trees), so this variable is the only way it reaches the build; configuring this preset without dot-sourcing light-env.ps1 first will fail to find a compiler.

compiler flags: Deliberately NOT pinned here. This preset briefly set PICO_COMMON_LANG_FLAGS to force the Zca/Zcb/Zcmp flag set, because pico_choose_compiler_flags() was falling through to a set without them. The real fault was in the probe, not in the flags, and it is fixed at the source instead: pico-sdk's riscv_zcmp_test.c listed s0 as an asm clobber, which GCC 15 refuses at the -O0 the probe compiles at, s0 being the frame pointer. So a probe for Zcmp support was failing for a reason unrelated to Zcmp support, on a toolchain that has it.

That is a local patch to the vendored pico-sdk (which already carries others), and it is the better fix: every RISC-V tree gets the right flags automatically, and the probe keeps its actual job of rejecting a toolchain whose assembler lacks the instructions -- verified both ways, it still fails correctly on a -march without zcmp.

For scale, so nobody re-litigates this for the size win: it is worth 489 UF2 blocks down to 485 on light_ui_demo_touch169 Debug, about 2KB or 0.8%. The alternative set is already rv32imaC with standard compression, so only the extra Zcb operations and Zcmp push/pop are new. This is unrelated to the ~17% by which the RISC-V image exceeds the ARM one, which spans two ISAs and two GCC versions.
Note that -mcpu=hazard3-rp2350, the list's FIRST entry, genuinely IS unsupported by this GCC (riscv-toolchain-15-x64-win, GCC 15.2.0). The probe is right to reject that one.
If flags ever do need pinning: CMAKE_<LANG>_FLAGS_INIT only applies on a first configure, so it needs a fresh build tree, not a reconfigure.

configurePresets.name: conf-screentest-mini-stm32h7-debug
configurePresets.description: WeAct MiniSTM32H7xx (STM32H743VIT6) on bare CMSIS. Inherits conf-light-base rather than conf-screentest-base: that base carries conf-light-pico-base, which sets LIGHT_SYSTEM=PICO_SDK and a PICO_SDK_PATH, neither of which means anything here. The arm-none-eabi toolchain is found on PATH by cmake/toolchain/arm_none_eabi.cmake, which light_preinit.cmake selects before project(); set LIGHT_TOOLCHAIN_PATH if more than one is installed and PATH order should not decide.

configurePresets.name: conf-screentest-trace
configurePresets.description: As conf-screentest-debug but at TRACE verbosity. conf-light-pico is inherited for the same reason it is there: it supplies LIGHT_PLATFORM and LIGHT_BOARD, and without a board light_platform.cmake has nothing to select a chip or toolchain from. This preset previously omitted it and could only configure by inheriting a board from whatever cache already occupied build/ -- so it appeared to work in a used tree and failed in a fresh one.

configurePresets.name: conf-screentest-release
configurePresets.description: As conf-screentest-debug but built for release. See conf-screentest-trace for why conf-light-pico is inherited and why this has its own binaryDir.
